Company description
AUGenomics is a women-owned next-generation sequencing laboratory based in San Diego. Beginning in 2023, we provide sequencing services and custom method development for academic, biotech, government, conservation and agricultural partners, with a focus on complex, tailored projects. We are deeply client-centric. We work as true partners to the researchers we support, staying in close contact throughout every project, troubleshooting alongside them, and treating their goals as our own. 
Job description
We are seeking a Laboratory Technician to lead a recurring high-volume DNA and RNA processing for agriculture and animal health, from weekly sample intake, extraction, library preparation, and Next Generation sequencing, with full responsibility for sample integrity and traceability. As an early member of a growing company, you will see directly how your work shapes the business and will have clear opportunities to expand your scope over time. Because this role works directly with our clients, including face-to-face, we are looking for someone who takes initiative and ownership of their projects as if they were their own, provides thoughtful and responsive customer service, genuinely cares about our clients and their research, and represents AUGenomics with professionalism, class and authenticity.
We are looking for a self-directed team player who takes pride in their work and brings strong attention to detail to every sample. The ideal candidate contributes to a positive, collaborative lab culture and is eager to learn across many areas, from bench work and sample tracking to SOP development. 
We are committed to protected time off and sustainable workloads, because balance and the prevention of burnout are central to how we operate. If you are excited by the opportunity to grow with a small, founder-led company, we encourage you to apply.
What you'll do
Sample intake:
receive weekly kit shipments, check them against tracking, inspect samples, and log every one with metadata. Flag anything missing, damaged or mislabeled the same day.
Batching and tracking:
organize samples into prep batches and keep our sample log and kit tracking sheets accurate and current. Every sample needs a clean chain of custody from box to data.
DNA extraction:
extract genomic DNA or RNA from complex environmental matrices, following our SOPs closely and consistently across high sample volumes.
Quality control:
measure DNA and/or RNA concentration and integrity (fluorometric quantification, DIN/RIN), record results, and make or escalate pass/fail calls.
Library preparation:
prepare NGS libraries, including adjusting steps like fragmentation based on sample QC, and hand off pooled libraries for sequencing.
Special handling and banking:
carry out client requests such as holding, freezing for RNA, or shipping backup samples to collaborators, and keep the banked-sample record up to date.
Lab upkeep:
manage reagent and consumable inventory for the program, maintain equipment, and keep the bench audit-ready.
Improve the process:
help refine SOPs, spot bottlenecks, and support new method work for this program (for example, viability testing and long-read sequencing).

What we're looking for
Bachelor's degree in biology, microbiology, molecular biology, biochemistry or a related field, or equivalent hands-on lab experience
Experience with core molecular techniques: pipetting, DNA extraction, PCR, and DNA quantification
Comfortable with repetitive, high-volume bench work without letting quality slip
Organized and detail-oriented.
Comfortable in Google Sheets or Excel, and willing to learn and help improve our Notion-based sample tracking and project portal systems
Comfort working with databases and structured data.
Clear communicator who flags problems early
Able to stand for extended periods and lift boxes up to 35 lbs

Nice to have
NGS library prep experience (Illumina, Element AVITI or similar)
Experience with environmental, soil, fecal or agricultural samples
Liquid handling robots or other automation
Work in a regulated or quality-focused lab (CLIA, GLP, ISO)
Programming or computer science experience (for example Python, R, SQL or scripting), and an interest in automating lab and data workflows

Benefits
Pay:
$26.44 to $31.25 per hour, based on experience, with a review at 6 months
Paid time off:
15 days PTO per year (with an additional 5 days Sick Leave). When you're out, you're out. No emails expected.
Paid holidays:
18 company holidays in 2026
Retirement:
401(k) with Roth option and a company match of up to 3.5% of salary (100% of the first 1% you contribute, plus 50% of the next 5%). Eligible after 3 months.
Training and growth:
hands-on training in NGS sample prep, library prep and lab operations, with a written growth plan and a clear path toward a Research Associate role
Location:
a lab in Sorrento Valley, San Diego, close to the biotech community

How to apply
To apply, email your resume to info@augenomics.com with "Laboratory Technician Application" in the subject line. Please include written responses to the following questions, a short paragraph each:
1. Tell us about a specific moment, class, project or experience that made you want to work in a lab. What happened, and why did it stay with you?
2. Where do you want your career to be in three to five years? Describe one concrete step you have already taken toward that goal.
3. Tell us about any specifics you’ve learned through education and any lab, technical or work experience that you believe have prepared you for this role.
4. Describe a previous lab or job you especially enjoyed. What made it a great experience, and what role did you play on that team?
Applications without responses to these questions will not be considered. We read every application thoughtfully and will reach out to candidates selected for an interview.

We consider all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 122,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.

Position Overview

The Senior Bioinformatics Scientist will serve as a technical lead and subject matter expert within the Minimal Residual Disease (MRD) program, working collaboratively with senior scientists and leaders on complex Research and Development projects. In this role, you will participate in or lead the planning of projects and analyses, and often act as the bioinformatics lead responsible for successful project execution. You will independently determine methods and procedures for new assignments, make detailed observations, analyze data, interpret results, and provide insights that shape the next steps and direction of the project. Your work will center on developing novel methods to identify and integrate genomic and epigenetic biomarkers that improve the sensitivity and specificity of MRD assays, contributing end-to-end across the data science workflow : collecting public datasets, curating internal data, forming hypotheses, building and validating models, and exploring machine learning and AI-based approaches. You will also research new technologies, contribute ideas and concepts to improve or develop processes, and help establish methods and workflows that advance product development toward diagnostic assay products.

Essential Duties

Include, but are not limited to, the following :

Technical leadership : Serve as bioinformatics lead and subject matter expert on one or more complex R&D projects, including those supporting diagnostic assay product development, and lead or participate in project and analysis planning.
Analysis and interpretation : Independently analyze experimental data across several product or technology areas, interpret results, identify trends, problems, and discrepancies, and recommend next steps and project direction.
Complex problem solving : Tackle problems of extremely complex scope where intangible variables must be evaluated, applying independent judgment to define methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria.
Method and study design : Independently develop methods, procedures, and development plans for new studies, and give technical input on project planning and experimental design.
Data and computational management : Manage bench-generated data and bioinformatics outputs in HPC or cloud computing environments, selecting and applying the right methods and technologies.
Data quality : Evaluate the impact of nonconforming data on products or processes and address trends in study data.
Innovation and IP : Track industry and technology developments, propose new techniques, lead process improvements, and contribute to the intellectual property portfolio.
Communication and presentation : Present and defend scientific findings at data, group, project, and departmental meetings, and communicate clearly with stakeholders at all levels, including functional managers and the clinical lab.
Documentation and compliance : Prepare and approve technical procedures, protocols, and reports, support abstracts, conferences, and publications, and follow legal, ISO, QSR, and Quality Management System requirements.
Mentorship and collaboration : Train and mentor research associates and junior scientists, foster a trusting, collaborative team environment, and manage multiple projects with shifting priorities.

Ph.D. in bioinformatics, computational biology, computer science, mathematics, or related field; or Master’s degree in bioinformatics, computational biology, computer science, mathematics, or related field plus 4 years of experience in lieu of a Ph.D.; or Bachelor’s degree in bioinformatics, computational biology, computer science, mathematics, or related field plus 6 years of experience in lieu of Ph.D.
